gloss: castle tower; main keep of a Japanese castle

definitions.explanation: The tall, central tower of a Japanese castle, serving as the final defensive stronghold and the symbolic centerpiece of the fortification. Typically a multi-storied structure with distinctive curved rooflines, it was the most visually striking element of castle architecture during the Sengoku and Edo periods.

examples.japanese: {姫路城|ひめじじょう}の{天守|てんしゅ}は{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The keep of Himeji Castle is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {天守|てんしゅ}の{最上階|さいじょうかい}からは{城下町|じょうかまち}が{一望|いちぼう}できる。
examples.english: You can see the entire castle town from the top floor of the keep.

examples.japanese: この{城|しろ}の{天守|てんしゅ}は{戦後|せんご}に{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリートで{再建|さいけん}されたものだ。
examples.english: This castle's keep was rebuilt with reinforced concrete after the war.

notes:
Also written as {天守閣|てんしゅかく}, which adds the suffix {閣|かく} ('tower; pavilion'). Both forms refer to the same structure, though {天守閣|てんしゅかく} is the more common form in everyday conversation and tourist contexts.

ETYMOLOGY:
- Castle keeps emerged during the late Muromachi and Sengoku periods (16th century) as military architecture evolved
- {織田|おだ}{信長|のぶなが}'s {安土城|あづちじょう} (1579) is considered the first grand-scale {天守|てんしゅ}
- Only twelve original {天守|てんしゅ} survive today; many others are reconstructions

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天守閣|てんしゅかく}: castle keep (with pavilion suffix; more common form)
- {天守|てんしゅ}に{登|のぼ}る: to climb the castle keep
- {現存|げんそん}{天守|てんしゅ}: surviving original keep
- {復元|ふくげん}{天守|てんしゅ}: reconstructed keep
- {天守台|てんしゅだい}: keep foundation/platform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {城|しろ}: castle — the general word for a castle as a whole, including walls, moats, and grounds
- {櫓|やぐら}: turret; watchtower — smaller defensive towers positioned at corners or along castle walls
- {本丸|ほんまる}: main bailey — the innermost fortified area of a castle where the keep stands
